eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper provides a structured interdisciplinary framework for effective human oversight and analyzes EU AI Act Article 14, directly relevant to governance and accountability in regulated high-risk AI. It does not specifically address LLMs or conversational systems in the provided text, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for a review focused on conversational governance in LLM-based systems.

Adequacy is moderate given the conceptual nature and limited visibility of full argumentative support in the excerpt.

coding.theme: Conditions and enablers of effective human oversight in high-risk AI
coding.subtheme: Alignment between conceptual oversight effectiveness and EU AI Act requirements

synthesis.main_claim: Effective human oversight of high-risk AI requires the oversight person to have sufficient causal power, suitable epistemic access, self-control, and fitting intentions; this is argued to be equivalent to being morally responsible with fitting intentions, with the main objective of oversight being risk mitigation.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an interdisciplinary understanding of effective human oversight integrating psychological, legal, philosophical, and technical perspectives; identifies facilitators and inhibitors across technical design, individual, and environmental domains; and scrutinizes EU AI Act Article 14 as an exemplary regulatory framework.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting conceptual and regulatory evidence on what makes human oversight effective in high-risk AI, including design factors such as intervention options, interface/interaction design, and runtime monitoring. Inform governance discussions on oversight, accountability, and compliance even where LLM or conversational specificity is not explicit.

evidence.claim: Paper focuses on effective human oversight as safeguard for high-risk AI
evidence.excerpt: Human oversight is currently discussed as a potential safeguard to counter some of the negative aspects of high-risk AI applications.

evidence.claim: Main objective of human oversight is risk mitigation
evidence.excerpt: Based on the claim that the main objective of human oversight is risk mitigation, we propose a viable understanding of effectiveness in human oversight

evidence.claim: Four conditions for effective human oversight
evidence.excerpt: for human oversight to be effective, the oversight person has to have (a) sufficient causal power with regard to the system and its effects, (b) suitable epistemic access to relevant aspects of the situation, (c) self-control, and (d) fitting intentions for their role.
an oversight person is effective if and only if they are morally responsible and have fitting intentions.

evidence.claim: Interdisciplinary method combining psychology, law, philosophy, and technical domains
evidence.excerpt: This paper investigates effective human oversight by synthesizing insights from psychological, legal, philosophical, and technical domains.

evidence.claim: Facilitators and inhibitors discussed across three domains
evidence.excerpt: We discuss factors in three domains, namely, the technical design of the system, individual factors of oversight persons, and the environmental circumstances in which they operate.

evidence.claim: EU AI Act Article 14 analyzed as regulatory exemplar
evidence.excerpt: this paper scrutinizes the upcoming AI Act of the European Union – in particular Article 14 on Human Oversight – as an exemplary regulatory framework
